In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a dip in the differential cross-section of γ p→ ηp in the momentum transfer region between zero and 2.0 GeV 2.
the data are in agreement with a smooth t-dependence of the differential cross-section.
the data do not support the existence of a resonance with a mass of around 1.6 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the η-meson is not produced in the t -channel in the momentum transfer region between 0 and 1.5 GeV.
the data are consistent with the predictions of the VDM model.
we have not seen any indication of the existence of a nucleon resonance around W=2.3 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the η-mesons are produced predominantly in the S-wave.
the differential cross section is well described by a simple Regge model with only one resonance in the t channel.
the data can be described with a simple Regge model with only one pole, the Pomeron.
